author: claude (research agent, clean-room)
status: our own rebuild, as a project file of our own schema, of the 13.92 s wave-2 export test timeline. No stored editor_state / autosave body of that timeline exists (the wave-2 recorder kept only app API bodies; W3-RF-08 notes say the same), so the numbers come from the sources listed under provenance, checked against our own frame measurements of the wave-2 export file.
cleanRoom: Numbers, our own field names and ids, Tears of Steel dialogue (CC BY 3.0, Blender Foundation) and the default text 'Heading'. No Xapp code, ids or document structure copied.
usedBy: EX-P11 frames vs the wave-2 export frames
OT-7 case W2-M25 (the caption request made on this timeline)
units: ms on the timeline unless a field says S (seconds); trim = source ms inside the fixture file; pixel values on the 1080 x 1920 canvas. Box convention (findings part 5 section 53.1.1): width / height = the UNSCALED box (for video the source's natural size), scale multiplies them; x / y = the top-left corner of the scaled, unrotated box; rendered size = width x scale by height x scale. Track order: tracks[].stackFromTop counts from the top (0 = top); the render order is bottom to top: V1, O1, C1 (findings part 5 section 53.5.1).

fade window [5477.236, 6477.236) ms, p = (frame / 30 x 1000 - 5477.236) / 1000. Each frame = opaque black, then one clip drawn over it at the alpha in fadeAlphas (findings part 5 section 55.5): frames 165-179 the speech picture (with its vignette) at cos(pi p), frames 180-194 the action picture at -cos(pi p). Expected pixel = round(alpha x that clip's own pixel), +-1 LSB. Frames 179 and 180 (alpha 0.0332 / 0.0715) are the two darkest; which of them is darker depends on the two pictures' levels, so the check compares per frame, not 'darkest'. Wave-2 measurement for reference: picture-area mean about 1 / 255 at frame 180.
